narrative: The model estimated an 82% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk prediction, not a certainty, but it was strong enough to lead to denial of your law school application. The factor that most strongly pushed the prediction toward failure was your third-year class standing: you are in the first decile, while accepted students average around the sixth decile. The second strongest factor was your first-year class standing, also first decile versus an accepted-student average near the sixth decile. Together, these two signals suggest sustained academic difficulty relative to successful applicants and were the main reasons the application was denied. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.20 was the third-most influential factor; because it is close to the accepted-student average of 3.23, it slightly pushed toward passing rather than failing, so it was not the cause of rejection, though it was not enough to offset the two standing signals. Next, request admissions feedback and ask whether human review or appeal is available. Address the weak class-standing record directly with an explanation and evidence of improvement, consider additional academic preparation and, if feasible, a stronger LSAT score, and apply to programs that evaluate context holistically.
